questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Function on Which to Apply a Root-Finding Method When Applying the Implicit Euler Method
questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}={x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,y(0)=1
$$

Using the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx=0.25,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step.
Which of the following is the **general form** of $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ in terms of the new values ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}},$ and the current value $y?$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2})\cdot 0.25 \\  & =0.25({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side and define the resulting expression as $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+0.25({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2} \\ {{0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-y-0.25({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.25$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-y-0.25({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}.
$$

Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x\,y-{y}^{2},\,y(0)=2
$$

Using the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx=0.25,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step.
Which of the following is the **general form** of $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ in terms of the new values ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}},$ and the current value $y?$
questions.worked_solution:

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =({x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2})\cdot 0.25 \\  & =0.25\,{x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side to define $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+0.25\,{x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2} \\ {{0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-0.25\,{x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-y}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.25$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-0.25\,{x}_{\text{new}}\,{y}_{\text{new}}-y.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{2}+x,\,y(0)=2
$$

Using the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx=1,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step.
Which of the following is the **specific function** $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ used in the first step?
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{x}_{\text{new}})\cdot 1 \\  & =({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{x}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side and define the resulting expression as $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{x}_{\text{new}} \\ {{{y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-y-{x}_{\text{new}}}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=1$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})={y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-y-{x}_{\text{new}}.
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=0+1=1.$ Therefore, the function used in the first step is

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-2-1 \\  & ={y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}={x}^{3}-xy,\,y(0.5)=1.1
$$

Use the implicit Euler method with one step and Newton's method to approximate $y(1).$ Round your answer to two decimal places.

$y(1)≈$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=1,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=1-0.5=0.5.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the implicit Euler method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}-{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}})\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.5({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}-0.5{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side and define the resulting expression as $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+0.5({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}-0.5{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the equation

$$
0.5{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}+{y}_{\text{new}}-y-0.5({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}=0.
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.5$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.5{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}+{y}_{\text{new}}-y-0.5({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}.
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=0.5+0.5=1.$ Then, the function $g$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & =0.5(1){y}_{\text{new}}+{y}_{\text{new}}-1.1-0.5(1)^{3} \\  & =1.5{y}_{\text{new}}-1.6.\end{aligned}
$$

We use a root-finding method with starting point $y=1.1$ to solve $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.$ We'll use Newton's method. 

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{g({y}_{\text{new}})}{{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})}
$$

Note that the derivative of $g$ is

$$
{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})=1.5.
$$

Therefore, our Newton's method iterative scheme is as follows:

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{1.5({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-1.6}{1.5}
$$

Applying several iterations of Newton's method starting with $y(0.5)=1.1,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}_{\text{new}})_{1} & =1.1 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{2} & ≈1.066667 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{3} & ≈1.066667\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y(1)≈1.07,$ rounded to two decimal places.

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{2}-3x,\,y(1.5)=-2.5
$$

Use the implicit Euler method with one step and Newton's method to approximate $y(2).$ Round your answer to two decimal places.

$y(2)≈$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=2,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=2-1.5=0.5.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the implicit Euler method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-3{x}_{\text{new}})\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-1.5{x}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side and define the resulting expression as $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-1.5{x}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the equation

$$
0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-{y}_{\text{new}}+y-1.5{x}_{\text{new}}=0.
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.5$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-{y}_{\text{new}}+y-1.5{x}_{\text{new}}.
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=1.5+0.5=2.$ Then, the function $g$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & =0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-{y}_{\text{new}}-2.5-1.5(2) \\  & =0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-{y}_{\text{new}}-5.5.\end{aligned}
$$

We use a root-finding method with starting point $y=-2.5$ to solve $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.$ We'll use Newton's method. 

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{g({y}_{\text{new}})}{{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})}
$$

Note that the derivative of $g$ is

$$
{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})=({y}_{\text{new}})-1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton's method iterative scheme is as follows:

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{0.5(({y}_{\text{new}})_{n})^{2}-({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-5.5}{(({y}_{\text{new}})_{n})-1}
$$

Applying several iterations of Newton's method starting with $y(1.5)=-2.5,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}_{\text{new}})_{1} & =-2.5 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{2} & =-2.464286 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{3} & ≈-2.464102 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{4} & ≈-2.464102\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y(2)≈-2.46,$ rounded to two decimal places.
